findings.title: Forgeable authorization token
findings.summary: OfflineAuthorizationToken could be directly instantiated with attacker-controlled values and the boundary treated isinstance(token, OfflineAuthorizationToken) as proof of authority; authority was self-attested, not independently authenticated.

findings.title: Caller-selected Git is not canonical authority
findings.summary: The authorization verifier accepted caller-supplied repository/commit/path/expected digest, so a throwaway repository with self-consistent attacker bytes satisfied it; the requester must never choose the trust root.

findings.title: Synthetic provenance must come from fixture evidence
findings.summary: The factory accepted arbitrary ForecastRows plus an arbitrary caller-named fixture identity and elevated them to OFFLINE_SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE verified provenance; hashing after labeling is provenance laundering, not proof of synthetic origin.

findings.title: Git anchor must bind the actual rows
findings.summary: The Git-anchored receipt authenticated blob A and separately hashed caller-presented rows B without establishing that A binds B; unrelated rows could borrow a blob's identity.

bounded_repair.scope: authority re-authentication against source-pinned canonical Git (CI-3 model), pinned synthetic fixture contract, artifact-bound Git-anchored row digests; frozen V0 bytes unchanged

remaining_findings.title: Keep the implementation decision from granting execution
remaining_findings.summary: The repaired boundary authenticates the implementation-only governance decision as if it were evaluation authority. That decision authorizes zero scientific-evaluation phases and records scientific_execution_authorized=false; therefore the execution path must remain fail-closed until a separately governed canonical evaluation authorization exists.
